issues.legal_issue: An exceptionally long delay in filing a written statement may be condoned only on a cogent and satisfactory explanation, and not merely because summons were served late or the equities are said to be balanced.
material_facts: The case was an appeal challenging an order that condoned delay in filing a written statement in a civil suit.
The court proceeded on the basis that summons had been served by 2009 and noted that the defendants had earlier appeared in the proceedings and obtained leave to defend.
Even counting from service in 2009, the written statement was filed more than five years late.
The defendants did not satisfactorily explain why they had failed to file the written statement after learning of the suit.
A related suit involved a similar application based on the same kind of explanation; that application had been rejected, and the rejection had been upheld on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, the order condoning the delay was set aside, and the application seeking condonation of delay was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the ordinary period for filing a written statement may be extended beyond the stated limit, but the discretion must be exercised only in exceptionally hard cases and not routinely. The defendant must plead and satisfactorily demonstrate a valid reason for the delay; procedural flexibility does not confer a right to take unlimited time, and balancing equities or invoking the procedural rules as handmaids of justice cannot replace a convincing explanation. The Court relied on Salem Advocate Bar Association, Tamil Nadu v. Union of India, (2005) 6 SCC 344, which held that the time limit is directory but extensions must not nullify it through routine exercise of discretion.

rule.if: appeal_from_late_written_statement_condonation and defendant_had_notice_of_suit and substantial_delay_in_filing_defence and not satisfactory_explanation_for_delay and similar_application_in_related_suit_was_rejected

predicates.appeal_from_late_written_statement_condo: A party appealed an order allowing a defendant to file a written statement after delay.
predicates.defendant_had_notice_of_suit: The defendant had notice of the suit through service of summons or participation in the proceedings.
predicates.substantial_delay_in_filing_defence: The defendant filed the written statement after a substantial period had passed from learning of the suit.
predicates.satisfactory_explanation_for_delay: The defendant gave a convincing and valid explanation for failing to file the written statement in time.
predicates.similar_application_in_related_suit_was_: A similar application in a related suit, based on the same kind of explanation, had been rejected.
predicates.condonation_order_set_aside_and_delay_ap: The appellate court set aside the order allowing the delayed filing and dismissed the application seeking permission to file late.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns permission to file a written statement late, the defendant had notice of the suit, the delay was substantial, no satisfactory explanation was given, and a similar application in a related suit was rejected, the condonation order is set aside and the delay application is dismissed.
